title: Naming collision: two different `PermissionSchema` exports cause downstream validators to reject all permission sets
body:
## Summary

`@objectstack/spec` exports **two distinct symbols named `PermissionSchema`**, in two different sub-paths:

| Export | Path | Shape | Intended use |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `PermissionSchema` | `@objectstack/spec/kernel` (`kernel/plugin-security-advanced.zod.ts`) | `{ id, resource, actions, scope, ... }` with `resource` enum `data.object` \| `ui.view` \| `system.config` \| ... | Plugin-sandbox permission declared in a plugin manifest |
| `PermissionSetSchema` | `@objectstack/spec/security` (`security/permission.zod.ts`) | `{ name, isProfile, objects, fields, tabPermissions, ... }` | Runtime-editable **metadata permission set** (the `permission` metadata type) |

This is a footgun. Downstream consumers that try to validate the `permission` metadata type by reaching for "the schema called `PermissionSchema`" pick the wrong one and end up rejecting every legal permission-set payload (every record fails with errors like `id: expected string, received undefined`, `resource: invalid option`, `actions: expected array`).

The framework's own canonical mapping is correct (see `packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-type-schemas.ts:95` — `permission: PermissionSetSchema`), but the naming collision makes it very easy to import the wrong one.

## Repro

```ts
// WRONG (what name-based search lands on first):
import { PermissionSchema } from '@objectstack/spec/kernel';
PermissionSchema.safeParse({ name: 'sales', isProfile: false, objects: { account: { allowRead: true } } });
// → 4 errors: id missing, resource invalid, actions missing, ...

// RIGHT:
import { PermissionSetSchema } from '@objectstack/spec/security';
PermissionSetSchema.safeParse({ name: 'sales', isProfile: false, objects: { account: { allowRead: true } } });
// → success
```

The server returns the correct schema via `/api/v1/meta` (also `PermissionSetSchema`), so the asymmetry only shows up on consumers that re-validate client-side.

## Real-world impact

Hit while wiring the studio metadata-admin create form in [`objectstack-ai/objectui`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui) (`packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/clientValidation.ts`). Workaround was a one-line import swap, but the next consumer will hit the same trap.

## Suggested fix (pick one)

1. **Rename** `kernel/plugin-security-advanced.zod.ts::PermissionSchema` → `PluginPermissionSchema` (or `SandboxPermissionSchema`). This is the smallest correct fix; the kernel one has clearly more specialized semantics.
2. Re-export both from the top-level barrel with **distinct names** and add an ESLint rule banning the ambiguous import.
3. Add a `/** @deprecated Use PluginPermissionSchema; for metadata, see PermissionSetSchema */` JSDoc tag on the kernel symbol now, plus a console warning when imported in dev.

Option 1 is the cleanest — the kernel schema is the more specialized one and was added later; the security one is the documented "permission set" of the metadata protocol.

## Affected files in framework

- `packages/spec/src/kernel/plugin-security-advanced.zod.ts:78` — defines the colliding `PermissionSchema`.
- `packages/spec/src/kernel/index.ts:24` — re-exports it from `@objectstack/spec/kernel`.
- `packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-type-schemas.ts:95` — uses `PermissionSetSchema` correctly (no change needed; documents intent).
- `packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts` — `PermissionSetSchema` (no change needed).

Happy to send a PR if you confirm the rename approach.
